# Prooptis

> Prooptis (Prooptis Μονοπρόσωπη Ι.Κ.Ε. / Prooptis Single Member P.C., Greece) helps Greek businesses in any sector set up and grow commercial activity in Switzerland: company establishment coordination and commercial development (finding Swiss buyers and partners). It does not work on investors or fundraising.

Prooptis is a Greek company (GEMI 195398703000, tax ID 803365672), founded in 2026. It is based in Greece. Its team has many years of experience from working in and running businesses in Switzerland, deep familiarity with the Swiss market, business culture and procedures, and a network of contacts in Switzerland. It passes this know-how on to clients in practice and through advice. It serves Greek companies of every sector (food and beverages, industry and machinery, agricultural products and equipment, software, B2B services and others) that want to sell in or establish themselves in Switzerland. Website languages: Greek (primary) and English.

## Services

- **Establishment in Switzerland (Εγκατάσταση στην Ελβετία):** coordination of company formation and procedures; introductions to Swiss lawyers, accountants, banks and insurers; tracking of deadlines and documents; premises search (office, warehouse, shop) where needed. Legal and tax advice is given by licensed partner professionals; Prooptis coordinates.
- **Commercial development (Εμπορική ανάπτυξη):** research and mapping of Swiss buyers, distributors and partners; first contacts and successive introductions through a network of contacts in Switzerland; outreach guidance (message, presentation, follow-up); customer expansion after the first clients. No guaranteed customers.

## How it works

1. Free intro call (δωρεάν κλήση γνωριμίας)
2. Needs assessment and written plan (steps, order, partners, timeline, expected third-party costs)
3. Execution with regular updates

Pricing is given as a written proposal per project after the intro call; third-party costs are shown separately.

- [Homepage (English)](https://prooptis.com/en/)
- [Articles (Greek)](https://prooptis.com/arthra/): practical guides for Greek businesses about Switzerland
- [Επιχείρηση στην Ελβετία: πώς ανοίγει εταιρεία μια ελληνική επιχείρηση](https://prooptis.com/arthra/etaireia-stin-elvetia/): GmbH vs AG vs branch, minimum capital, commercial register, Swiss-resident signatory, bank, steps, timeline, common mistakes
- [Φόροι, ΦΠΑ και εισφορές στην Ελβετία](https://prooptis.com/arthra/foroi-fpa-elvetia/): federal/cantonal/communal profit tax, effective rates by canton, Swiss VAT (8.1%, CHF 100,000 worldwide threshold), social contributions, Greece–Switzerland double tax treaty (general information, not tax advice)
- [Πώς βρίσκει πελάτες και συνεργάτες στην Ελβετία μια ελληνική επιχείρηση](https://prooptis.com/arthra/pelates-stin-elvetia/): language regions, trade fairs, chambers and agencies, Swiss B2B culture, outreach and trust, localising the offer
- [Εξαγωγές στην Ελβετία: τελωνείο, δασμοί και ΦΠΑ εισαγωγής, βήμα βήμα](https://prooptis.com/arthra/exagoges-stin-elvetia/): exporting goods from Greece to Switzerland: export and import declarations, zero Swiss duty on industrial goods since 1 January 2024 (food and agricultural goods still dutiable), Swiss import VAT (8.1% / 2.6%), proof of origin, small consignments and online sales, Incoterms DAP vs DDP, food labelling rules, the Passar customs system (general information, not customs or tax advice)
- [Υποκατάστημα ή θυγατρική στην Ελβετία: τι συμφέρει μια ελληνική επιχείρηση](https://prooptis.com/arthra/ypokatastima-i-thygatriki-elvetia/): branch vs Swiss GmbH/AG subsidiary: liability, minimum capital (GmbH CHF 20,000 fully paid, AG CHF 100,000 with at least CHF 50,000 paid in, branch none), commercial register, Swiss-resident signatory, profit tax, VAT CHF 100,000 worldwide threshold, and the Greece–Switzerland double tax treaty on dividends vs profit transfer (general information, not legal or tax advice)
- [Υπηρεσίες σε Ελβετούς πελάτες από την Ελλάδα: τι πρέπει να ξέρετε](https://prooptis.com/arthra/ypiresies-gia-elvetous-pelates/): selling services from Greece to Swiss business clients without a Swiss entity: place of supply (recipient's seat) and invoicing without Greek VAT, Swiss acquisition tax (Bezugsteuer) borne by the Swiss recipient, when Swiss VAT registration applies (CHF 100,000 worldwide turnover), the notification procedure for working in Switzerland (up to 90 days per year, notice at least 8 days in advance), posting rules, and permanent establishment under the Greece–Switzerland double tax treaty (general information, not legal or tax advice)
